title: Predictive interaction-edge encoder with native world-action diffusion
coverage_gap: With only one LL and one HH trajectory, an unrestricted raw-state model can conflate cabinet side with yaw and memorize the timing of the raised approach. The support contains almost no independent layout variation or off-trajectory contact recovery.
reusable_regularity: Share a learned edge operator across hand-to-handle, handle-to-goal, and hand-to-goal relations. Each edge sees its displacement in world and cabinet coordinates, observed relative increment, distance, and a fixed role tag. A small fused latent is trained both by action diffusion and by predicting future hand/handle relations. The forecast objective asks the encoder to capture reach, descent and actual drawer response rather than merely identify a layout. Unlike analytical action canonicalization, native world axes are retained at the denoiser output to accommodate the fixed robot, gripper and native cube.
dependencies_preserved: The 36-dimensional direct physical bypass includes world and local hand-handle and goal-handle vectors, world hand/handle increments, world hand and goal coordinates, yaw, current/previous quaternions, aperture and aperture change. Learned compression cannot erase these explicit dependencies.
The shared edge MLP has role tags, so reaching the handle is not confused with pulling it to the goal; no permutation-invariance assumption erases the hand/object/goal roles.

Absolute hand and goal, drawer relations and yaw retain the task-varying cabinet geometry and robot workspace. The fixed end-effector frame is respected by native world action encoding. There is no obstacle planner or extra geometry source.
Native previous fields and two whole histories retain observed motion. Absent object2 zeros are omitted, not treated as an obstacle.

evidence_refs.detail: Exact two-episode support and sixteen-frame capability; no other layouts or feedback available.
Fixed native orientation, state-only policy, shared handle/goal/yaw fields, 16-step prediction and four-step execution specified by the public contract.
One LL and one HH; comparable 0.128 m initial pull lengths despite opposite horizontal directions; gripper action is -1 throughout the two supports, but this is not hard-coded.
Raised approach motivates learning the response beyond instantaneous distance alone.
Hand descends along the cabinet face before pulling.
Interaction stage near the low handle.
Same broad raised-approach structure in the other signed layout.
Hand near the handle immediately before/at pulling in demo 01.
Actions 0:28 and 40:72 and observations 62:70 show a sharp action-stage change while the handle is initially static.
Observations 63:68 show a similarly small hand-handle gap and static handle at the onset of pull.
Two histories, 16 native actions, four executed, auxiliary objectives must be separately mask-normalized.

expected_failure_signature: Forecast supervision should reduce phase ambiguity if the future relation is predictable from causal geometry. If it instead memorizes support timing, the policy will lower/pull at the wrong location when approach duration changes.

The world-action model must learn yaw-dependent action components; extreme-yaw failure with decent crossed-cell behavior would falsify the sufficiency of dual-coordinate edge encoding without output equivariance.

A training-only forecast can become good on support without helping actual contact. The resulting signature would be repeated commanded pulling while the observed drawer fails to move; no predicted state is treated as a runtime observation.

required_runtime_fields.fields: 0:11 current hand/aperture/handle/quaternion; 18:29 native previous equivalents; 36:39 goal; 39:41 cabinet yaw sine/cosine

action_frame_semantics: Identity encode/decode of all four native action channels. XYZ remain world displacement commands with native 0.01 m scale; gripper remains its separate signed actuator command. Only the public executor clips native [-1,1] and executes four of sixteen actions. Yaw rotation is used for features and auxiliary targets only, never as an undisclosed action transform.

training_only_targets.name: future_relations
training_only_targets.source_fields: For valid t+k<T, obs[t+k+1,0:3] minus obs[t+k+1,4:7], and obs[t+k+1,4:7] minus obs[t,4:7]. Both rotated by the causal start yaw obs[t,39:41], then divided by 0.1 m. Only the exact supplied support episodes are used.
training_only_targets.loss: Forecast head maps both causal conditioning rows to 16x6 labels. Squared error multiplied by batch.mask[...,None], divided by mask.sum()*6 (clamped denominator for an all-zero mask), weight 0.1. Padded labels are zero and masked. Common action4 epsilon loss remains weight 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4.
training_only_targets.inference_exclusion: The forecast head is called only in training_loss. No labels, masks, future observation, episode identity or time index enter condition, denoise, or action encode/decode. No forecast is supplied as future truth at deployment.

support_fit_statistics: None. Metric scaling is fixed in code/config, common normalization and all frozen trainer settings remain unchanged. No support cache is retained on the design.
architecture: Shared 13->64->32 SiLU edge encoder, concatenated three edges plus 36 physical features ->128->48 latent. Condition is 48 latent + 36 physical =84 per observation. One unchanged common action4 DP. Training-only (2*84)->128->96 forecast head. All modules registered during build_modules and trained by the joint loss; no extra updates or pretraining.
change_summary: Initial design, not a performance revision: native world action diffusion with shared learned relational representation and a separately normalized training-only future-geometry loss. No checks or results from training/evaluation used.
